records.title: A two-dimensional complex with embedding-dimension gap two
records.description:
This research note proves the existence of a finite two-dimensional simplicial complex with minimum piecewise-linear embedding dimension three and minimum original-simplex affine embedding dimension five. It answers affirmatively Brehm's 2006 question whether these minimum embedding dimensions can differ by more than one, already in dimension two. The first barycentric subdivision embeds linearly in three dimensions.

The argument makes a known balanced-Radon and random-complex affine obstruction uniform under all small facet deletions, then removes triangles sharing an edge. An elementary local-fan construction supplies the PL embedding. Existing Brehm–Sarkaria, Newman and Lee–Nevo methods are credited. Two independently fixed bounded literature audits found no checked theorem subsuming this exact result; categorical first priority is not asserted. Exact finite parameters and independent offline checks are supplied, but no explicit facet list for the enormous witness is generated. Finite checks supplement the universal proof and are not formal verification.

Generative AI tools were used extensively in problem solving, proof checking, literature review, manuscript preparation and independent adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint; no human peer review or formally machine-verified proof is claimed. Research prose is licensed CC BY4.0 and verification code MIT. The source-and-verification archive contains the manuscript source, pinned standard-library checks, provenance and source/priority evidence. The repository publication program records the separate fresh full preprint reviews.

records.title: The vertex centroid of focal antipedals of even elliptic billiards
records.description:
We prove invariant k405 for the original-polygon, full-line antipedals of elliptic billiards with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic and even least period. The unweighted vertex centroid is zero for the center pole and has an explicit phase-independent focal coefficient determined by the axes, caustic parameter, period and perimeter. The proof covers primitive star polygons and either orientation; the circle is treated separately. Repeated odd polygons with even list length and hyperbolic or degenerate caustics are outside the theorem. A self-contained finite-action and perimeter-stationarity proof and portable exact verification supplement are supplied.

This answers k405 as posed without proof in Reznik-Garcia-Koiller's 2020/2021 source. Ferudun's later deposited note, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23092466, states the same theorem and coefficient and uses the same pair-and-moment mechanism; that overlap is explicitly credited. A proof was publicly posted in PR140 on September 30, 2026, before the specific overlapping Zenodo record was created on October 1. The bounded primary-source audit did not establish an earlier complete answer. No absolute priority, exclusive theorem novelty, independent-discovery, copying or collaboration claim is made. The problem is not described as still unsolved at this note's publication.

AI tools were used extensively in developing, drafting, reproducing and adversarially auditing this work. Independent AI reviews are not conventional human peer review. This preprint is unrefereed and has not undergone conventional human peer review.

records.title: The outer-pedal area centroid in even-period elliptic billiards
records.description: We prove the k307 outer-side pedal area-centroid observation of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller for billiards in a noncircular ellipse with a strict confocal elliptic caustic and least even period. The ordered perpendicular feet of any fixed point on the boundary tangent lines have an explicit phase-independent signed area centroid wherever their signed area is nonzero. We classify the entire zero-area locus: none when d is nonnegative, and a fixed circle when d is negative. Simple winding-one even families have a centroid for every fixed point; the four-period value is M/3. An exact primitive eight-period star shows that the exceptional undefined locus is real. The note supplies an all-period support-coordinate and cubic-moment proof. The verification archive contains the LaTeX source, exact symbolic and rational certificates, independent high-precision orbit controls, audit reports and reproducibility instructions. The original observation and classical methods are credited. Bounded primary-source audits found no earlier covering proof, without certifying historical firstness. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, literature research, writing and adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint and has not received external human peer review or proof-assistant formalization.
